purpose: Candidate discovery SOURCE CATALOG, not a list of lead companies and not permission to scrape directory websites.
scope: Worldwide frontend studio campaign excluding India; secondary sources for other configured ICPs.

constraints.commercial_crawling: Do not add an automated directory crawler without checking its robots.txt, relevant terms, licensing, and documented API or explicit permission.
constraints.manual_import: Review directory listings manually, collect official agency name and its own website, and feed those records through the existing manual_csv source (name,url).
constraints.provenance: Keep source directory attribution in human review records; the current manual_csv adapter does not preserve individual directory provenance without additional work.
constraints.verification: Do not treat directory statements as first-party proof of offered services, location, headcount, leaders or React/Next.js capabilities.
constraints.deduplication: Deduplicate by canonical company domain and keep a separate source occurrence log.
constraints.safety: Honor source limits; no email extraction, guessed contacts, automated sending, bypassing blocks, or paid APIs in the $0 pilot.
constraints.evidence: No measured live yield is claimed for any of the new directories. Selection order is a hypothesis to validate with small labeled batches.

evaluated_sources.reason: Documented `industry` filter (openapi.json) lets one of the 3 bounded queries target studios serving SaaS clients instead of repeating a free-text variant of the category query. Unmeasured hypothesis: exposed as --pickanagency-profile complementary, default unchanged until a live A/B shows more human-relevant studios per request.

The documented search API has no offset/page/cursor/sort parameter and limit caps at 25, so one query can never return more than 25 records. Bulk or extra fields require contacting the provider (hello@pickanagency.com).

Field filtering is documented (e.g. field_org_membership_status). It would drop dormant listings but also every non-member studio; the effect on relevant-studio yield is unknown. Organization nodes have no documented size/services fields.

GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies and Terms prohibit using information collected from the service, including through the API, for spamming/unsolicited solicitation. This product's purpose is outbound prospecting, so GitHub-derived company lists are a policy risk even though the API is free.

Every request needs a registered API key (free, but a key is outside the keyless $0 pilot approval), and the register is UK-only. SIC 62012 would find software companies but the register carries no website or headcount, so first-party domains could not be derived without guessing.

No documented free API or permission to collect was found in the existing catalog review; these domains are already treated as non-first-party. Not re-verified in this session. Use manual review via directory_seed only.
Finding studios by content would require downloading WARC data in bulk, which this task forbids; the URL index alone cannot identify software studios. Not tested.

Other Wikidata classes (e.g. web development or IT-consulting companies) could not have their Q-ids verified offline. WikidataAdapter fails closed on label mismatch, so a class should only be added together with a live label check and a COUNT query; thin studio coverage is expected either way.
